# Report: Famaey & McGaugh, "MOND: Observational Phenomenology and Relativistic Extensions"

## 1. The question, frozen
The title and opening make one question central: **why do the motions of galaxies exceed what their visible stars and gas predict, and does a single law with a critical acceleration a₀ account for the pattern?** (The paper answers more — how to embed it relativistically — but that is downstream.) Range: from galaxy scales out (the paper also touches clusters and cosmology). Since galaxies cannot be poked, the change list is made of comparisons: other masses, other surface densities, other environments.

## 2. The explanation in parts
In the owners' words: (a) a critical acceleration a₀ ≈ 10⁻¹⁰ m s⁻², with a₀ ≈ cH₀/2π and a₀² ~ Λ; (b) below a₀, a = √(a₀ g_N) ("deep MOND"), which gives V⁴ = G M a₀; (c) the baryonic Tully–Fisher relation, slope 4, zero point ≈ G a₀; (d) no residual with baryonic surface density Σ_b; (e) the mass-discrepancy–acceleration relation, D ∝ 1/√(g_N/a₀); (f) an interpolating function μ(x); (g) the external field effect (EFE); (h) relativistic extensions (TeVeS, GEA, BIMOND…); (i) a ~2 eV neutrino patch for clusters; (j) modified inertia *vs* modified gravity.

## 3. Part by part

| Part | Mark | Held by / what would settle it |
|---|---|---|
| (a) value of a₀ | **Fixed** | Owner set it; fitted to the same galaxy data it explains. Not derived. |
| (a) a₀ ≈ cH₀, a₀² ~ Λ | **Unknown** | No test yet. Settled by a deeper theory deriving a₀ from cosmology. |
| (b) deep-MOND relation | **Held** | Breaks the flat-curve, BTFR-zero-point and mass-discrepancy jobs if changed. Built: it predicted tidal dwarfs before they were checked. |
| (c) BTFR slope 4 | **Held** | The slope falls out of (b); changing it breaks the fit. Slope 3 (the dark-matter expectation) would kill it. |
| (d) no Σ_b residual | **Held** | The poke — hold mass, change surface density, V unchanged — was tried and confirmed. Hard to vary. |
| (e) D-relation | **Held** | By the mass-discrepancy job. Careful: the owners say it is *not* independent of (c). |
| (f) interpolating function | **Loose** | Any smooth μ with the right asymptotes does the same work. The asymptotes are held; the shape is free. |
| (g) external field effect | **Held if** | Rests on an unconfirmed job — that a galaxy's environment alters its internal dynamics. Settled by a dwarf in a strong external field. |
| (h) relativistic extensions | **Unknown** | Many attempts, none complete. Settled by one theory matching lensing *and* the CMB *and* galaxy curves. |
| (i) cluster neutrino patch | **Held if** | Allowed only if a ~2 eV sterile neutrino exists. Its gauge is direct detection. |
| (j) inertia vs gravity | **Two routes** | Both reproduce the non-relativistic law alone; they part company on the EFE. |

## 4. Whole-explanation checks
**Flip.** Had rotation curves fallen Keplerianly, (b)–(e) would all be dead. They do not, so the flip is survived — a real test.

**Direction.** The slope-4 BTFR is *derived* from a₀, not read off the fit — the right direction. But a₀'s *value* is reverse-fitted from the very data it explains, and its coincidence with cH₀ is a separate, unexplained fact.

**Answer hidden in the starting points.** a₀ is the answer placed in the starting point. The owners are honest that a₀ ~ cH₀/2π is a "coincidence… remains an open question" — that is the loose seam.

**Where the jobs came from.** Most jobs are the owners' own, framed in MOND's language ("a₀ appears in *five roles*"). That framing is fair here because the same observations are also ΛCDM's problems — but note the jobs are assembled by MOND's advocates, so a job like "why the same a₀ in unrelated relations" is partly built by them. It is a good added job: it kills most rival versions.

**Pairs that pull.** Two stand out. (1) The "no dark matter" claim against the cluster neutrino patch (i): adding mass back to fit clusters partly undoes the selling point. (2) γ (galaxies) against cosmology: a₀ fixes galaxy curves but says nothing about the CMB third peak, so the relativistic part must carry it. The paper says which side gives way — galaxies hold, cosmology is patched.

**Catch-alls and gauges.** On the ΛCDM side, "gastrophysics/feedback" absorbs the cusp-core and missing-baryon failures with no gauge — the owners rightly press this. On the MOND side, the neutrino patch (i) has a gauge (detection), so it is a legitimate patch, not a catch-all. The interpolating function (f) is a free function, not a catch-all — allowed.

**What the change list leaves out.** Cluster masses (MOND undershoots), lensing mass in clusters, and the CMB. These are left out *openly*, as stated problems — so the narrowed range is honest, not smuggled.

**Rivals.** MOND and ΛCDM are told apart by one change: take a galaxy at a < a₀ with an unusual baryon distribution. MOND predicts V from the baryons alone; ΛCDM does not. The paper's Figure 5 is that test, and MOND passes it. If a future baryon-feedback model reproduced the same regularities, the two would be the same at this level.

**Where the parts came from.** Fitted: a₀'s value, the μ shape, the neutrino mass. Built: the deep-MOND relation and its BTFR prediction — it stuck its neck out on tidal dwarfs and was caught out *confirming*, the strongest kind. Asserted: that MOND is one "universal force law," and the relativistic embeddings.

## 5. What would make it harder to vary
1. A derivation of a₀ (why a₀² ~ Λ), turning the biggest loose end into a held one.
2. A decisive EFE test — currently "held if."
3. A completed relativistic theory that *predicts* the CMB and lensing rather than patching them.

## 6. What this does not show
Passing the checks is not truth. MOND could be a faithful phenomenological law that a dark-matter theory with a fifth force eventually reproduces — the owners say so themselves. Hard to vary is a mark of a good explanation, not a proof of a true one.

## 7. One next step
Run the EFE poke: find a low-acceleration dwarf inside a strong external field and check whether its internal dynamics shift as MOND's EFE predicts. It is the one clean cut that could move (g) from "held if" to "held."
